From: MARK TRAMO  
To: Lesley Groff < 
>, Jeffrey Epstein
Subject: Re: Journal of Interdisciplinary Music Studies (JIMS)1 Advisory Board 
Date: Sun, 11 Jun 2017 19:15:06 +0000 
Thanks, JEE - provocative...inspiring these thoughts and consideration in my book - 
You wrote "how and why" music is created. Candidate titles for my book with ICM's Kris Dahl: 
"Why Music? Human Sociobiology and Communication." or 
"The Music Instinct: Mind, Brain and Culture." 
I. Your insight on reverse-engineering music resonates with Al Liberman's "Motor Theory of Speech 
Perception". The emphasis there is the dependence of speech perception on our motivation and ability to create 
and produce speech. So moving our mouths and feeling our mouths move when we speak to communicate OUR 
thoughts and feelings emotions is correlated with hearing what we produce. Having learned to do this for 
ourselves, we then apply the same multi-modal system to decoding the acoustic signals of others who are trying 
to communicate THEIR thoughts and feelings. 
2. I've been thinking about music in relation to communication in general, including animal communication, 
especially apes and monkeys. Recently read some relevant sections by Darwin in "Origin..." and "Emotional 
Expression..." The "how" of both language and music must reflect both unique properties of the human nervous 
system (e.g., an unprecedented expansion of the anterior frontal lobe with its agranular cytoarchitecture and 
widespread connectivity) and universal properties we share with all mammals who use sound to communicate to 
one another. 
3. You emphasized "how and why" music is created. Would you please give me some feedback re: your take on 
the candidate titles for my book with ICM's Kris Dahl: 
A. "Why Music? Human Sociobiology and Communication." 
B. "The Music Instinct: Mind, Brain and Culture." 
Best, 
Mark

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish at Home 
for the Elton John AIDS Foundation 
THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a truly memorable event. With inspiration from the then U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, and soaring arias from the magnificent Andrea Bocelli and Maria Aleida, plus mind boggling magic from Uor Suchard, 
all sewn together by our emcee David Walliams, it was one of the happiest evenings we can remember at our home. 
This year's Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the generous support of our friends at BVLGARI, promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary performer loan Baez, who has not only created her own iconic classics, but has fabulously reinterpreted music by everyone from Bob Dylan and Stevie Wonder to the Rolling Stones, Ryan Adams and Josh Ritter, will 
perform for us. Elton is looking forward to sharing a stage with her for the first time ever. The wonderful David Walllams will look after us as emcee and we have some very special VIP guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the Woodside Gallery Dinner do so much good. You may remember a young man named Leslie who spoke at last years event. When he was a child, Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. He was at her bedside. 
Today, Leslie works to educate the LGBT community in South Africa about HIV. He travels to townships and slums, providing HIV testing and referring those who need it to clinics where they will not be shamed or turned away. Thanks to your generosity, 
this work has expanded to 200 clinics nationally. We visited one In July with the South African Minister of Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us that the success of these services in preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS is helping the South African 
government to now afford funding all medical HIV treatment for its people without external support. 
Also last July, tickled HRH Prince Harry onstage at the International AIDS Conference in Durban to talk about the critical need to help adolescents living with HIV. We urged the international community not to give up on this precious group when we 
have had so much success fighting the epidemic amongst adults, mothers and babies. Reaching adolescents is our last huge global challenge in the fight against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues that call for our attention today. I cannot tell you how grateful David and I and everyone at the Foundation are that you continue to share our passion and our vision for a future where AIDS is not something our 
children or our grandchildren will have to worry about. Healthy societies, at home and abroad, mean less instability or dependence on others. We believe it is not only possible but essential. 
We do hope you will join us in June so we can continue the work of the Foundation. You can download your invitation to purchase tickets to this year's Woodside Gallery Dinner below. 
With your support, we will fight the stigma, stop new infections and save countless lives. 
In the meantime, if you need any further information on the Woodside Gallery Dinner, please do not hesitate to contact Glenn Horder at the Foundation as per contact details below. 
With our warmest regards, 
Elton John 
David Furnish 
Founder 
Chairman

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish at Home 
for the Elton John AIDS Foundation 
THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a truly memorable event. With inspiration from the then U.S. Secretary 
of State John Kerry, and soaring arias from the magnificent Andrea Bocelli and Maria Aleida, plus mind boggling 
magic from Lior Suchard, all sewn together by our emcee David Walliams, it was one of the happiest evenings we can 
remember at our home. 
This year's Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the generous support of our friends at BVLGARI, promises to be as 
magical. 
We are so excited that legendary performer Joan Baez, who has not only created her own iconic classics, but has 
fabulously reinterpreted music by everyone from Bob Dylan and Stevie Wonder to the Rolling Stones, Ryan Adams 
and Josh Ritter, will perform for us. Elton is looking forward to sharing a stage with her for the first time ever. The 
wonderful David Walliams will look after us as emcee and we have some very special VIP guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the Woodside Gallery Dinner do so much good. You may remember a young 
man named Leslie who spoke at last year's event. When he was a child, Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. He was at 
her bedside. Today, Leslie works to educate the LGBT community in South Africa about HIV. He travels to townships 
and slums, providing HIV testing and referring those who need it to clinics where they will not be shamed or turned 
away. Thanks to your generosity, this work has expanded to 200 clinics nationally. We visited one in July with the 
South African Minister of Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us that the success of these services in preventing the 
spread of HIV/AIDS is helping the South African government to now afford funding all medical HIV treatment for its 
people without external support.

critical need to help adolescents living with HIV. We urged the international community not to give up on this

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish at Home 
for the Elton John AIDS Foundation 
THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a truly memorable event. With inspiration from the then U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, and soaring arias from the magnificent Andrea Bocelh and Maria Aleida, plus mind boggling magic from We 
Suchard, all sewn together by our emcee David Walliams, it was one of the happiest evenings we can remember at our home. 
This years Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the generous support of our friends at BVLGARI, promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary performer loan Baez, who has not only created her own iconic classics, but has fabulously reinterpreted music by everyone from Bob Dylan and Stevie Wonder to the Rolling Stones, Ryan Adams and Josh Ritter, 
will perform for us. Elton is looking forward to shanng a stage with her for the first time ever. The wonderful David Walllams will look after us as emcee and we have some very special VIP guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the Woodside Gallery Dinner do so much good. You may remember a young man named Leslie who spoke at last year's event. When he was a child, Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. He was at her 
bedside. Today, Leslie works to educate the LGBT community in South Africa about HIV. He travels to townships and slums, providing HIV testing and referring those who need it to clinics where they will not be shamed or turned away. Thanks to 
your generosity, this work has expanded to 200 clinics nationally. We visited one in July with the South African Minister of Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us that the success of these services in preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS is helping 
the South African government to now afford funding all medical HIV treatment for its people without external support. 
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince Harry onstage at the International AIDS Conference in Durban to talk about the critical need to help adolescents living with HIV. We urged the international community not to give up on this precious group when 
we have had so much success fighting the epidemic amongst adults, mothers and babies. Reaching adolescents is our last huge global challenge in the fight against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues that call for our attention today. I cannot tell you how grateful David and I and everyone at the Foundation are that you continue to share our passion and our vision for a future where AIDS is not something our 
children or our grandchildren will have to worry about. Healthy societies, at home and abroad, mean less instability or dependence on others. We believe it is not only possible but essential. 
We do hope you will pain us in June so we can continue the work of the Foundation. You can download your invitation to purchase tickets to this years Woodside Gallery Dinner below. 
With your support, we will fight the stigma, stop new infections and save countless lives. 
In the meantime, if you need any further information on the Woodside Gallery Dinner, please do not hesitate to contact Glenn Harder at the Foundation as per contact details below. 
With our warmest regards, 
Elton John 
David Furnish 
Founder

I am writing on behalf of Richard Parncutt at the Centre for Systematic Musicology in Graz. We would like 
to thank you for your continuing support of the Journal of Interdisciplinary Music Studies (JIMS) as a 
member of the Advisory Board. 
The last few years have been quiet, but we recently published a Special Issue entitled 'Cognition of Early 
Polyphony', edited by Frans Wiering and Barbara Tillmann. We also renewed our homepage at 
http://www.musicstudies.org, so please take a look and download one of the latest articles if you like 
(open access). We will advertise the journal at conferences over the summer (see attached flyer) and 
expect to receive more submissions in the coming academic year. 
We are also updating the editorial boards and would like to continue to list you as a member of the 
Advisory Board. Please let us know if that is appropriate for you. You will not be required to do anything in 
return for having your name listed, but we may ask you to be action editor or anonymous reviewer for a 
future submission. 
Thank you very much and best wishes, 
Maximilian Burkard 
(student assistant)

Mark Jude Tramo, MD PhD
